propositions.text: The appellant family are Angolan citizens fearing persecution due to refusal of a forced marriage proposal by in-laws.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX and Ms. XXXX, you and your children are citizens of Angola, and you state that you fear persecution in your country, when your in-laws, Sir, wanted your eldest daughter to marry one of your uncles, Madam, which you refused.

propositions.text: In-laws became violent and sent criminals to threaten the family after refusal.
propositions.quote: As a result, the in-laws became violent and sent criminals to threaten you.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant family fears persecution in Angola due to refusal of a forced marriage, leading to violent threats by in-laws.

propositions.text: The father acts as designated representative for his minor children.
propositions.quote: Sir, you are acting as the designated representative of your minor children.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the father is the designated representative for his minor children.

propositions.text: The Refugee Protection Division rejected the refugee protection claims due to lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejected your refugee protection claims after finding that you were not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the appellant not credible and rejected the refugee claims.

propositions.text: On appeal, the appellant submitted evidence, requested an oral hearing, and argued RPD erred on credibility.
propositions.quote: On appeal, you submitted evidence, requested that an oral hearing be held and argue that the RPD committed errors regarding your credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues on appeal that the RPD erred on credibility and requests an oral hearing with new evidence.

propositions.text: The documentary evidence submitted on appeal was inadmissible and an oral hearing was impossible.
propositions.quote: After analyzing your file, I concluded that the documentary evidence submitted on appeal was not admissible and that it was impossible to hold a hearing.

propositions.text: The RPD did not commit the errors alleged by the appellant.
propositions.quote: I also concluded that the RPD did not commit the errors you criticize it for.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the new evidence inadmissible, an oral hearing impossible, and no RPD errors were made.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed based on the conclusions reached.
propositions.quote: In light of these conclusions, your appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal based on its conclusions.

propositions.text: RAD Rules require appellants to provide detailed submissions on documentary evidence admissibility under IRPA subsection 110(4).
propositions.quote: The Rules of the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD Rules) set out that the person who is the subject of the appeal must provide in his memorandum full and detailed submissions of how any documentary evidence that he wants to raise on appeal meets the requirements of subsection 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and how that evidence relates to the appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD Rules require detailed submissions on documentary evidence admissibility under IRPA 110(4).

propositions.text: The appellant argues the written testimony meets IRPA 110(4) as it was obtained post-RPD hearing and relates to the appellant.
propositions.quote: In your memorandum, you argue that this written testimony satisfies the requirements of subsection 110(4) because they were obtained after the hearing before the RPD and that at the time of that hearing, none of the in-laws had dared testify about this situation out of fear of retaliation.

propositions.text: The appellant states the cousin was convinced to testify and has knowledge of the situation since the start.
propositions.quote: You also submit that you had to convince this cousin so that he would agree to testify and that this testimony has a tie to you because he is your wife's cousin and that he had been aware of this situation since the start until now.

propositions.text: The appellant states he submitted evidence referred to in IRPA 110(4) included in written testimony.
propositions.quote: In your written statement, Mr. XXXX, you state that you submitted evidence referred to in subsection 110(4) of the IRPA, which are included in written testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the written testimony meets IRPA 110(4) requirements and relates to the appellant, obtained post-RPD hearing.

propositions.text: RAD must generally proceed without a hearing on RPD record; subsection 110(4) creates limited exceptions for new evidence.
propositions.quote: I find it necessary to point out that subsection 110(3) of the IRPA explicitly sets out that, generally, the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) must proceed without a hearing on the basis of the record of the proceedings of the RPD. Subsection 110(4) creates an exception to this general rule.

propositions.text: Admissibility criteria for new evidence preserve process integrity and finality at first decision level.
propositions.quote: The existence of criteria governing the admissibility of new evidence on appeal helps to preserve the integrity of the process by promoting finality with respect to the factual record at the first level of decision-making, with very limited exceptions, and encouraging the narrowing of issues as matters move up the appellate ladder.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD generally proceeds without hearing on RPD record; new evidence admissibility criteria preserve process integrity and finality.

propositions.text: The cousin's written testimony describes threats and violent attacks by uncle and criminals after refusal of marriage proposal.
propositions.quote: In the written testimony dated XXXX 19, 2020, your cousin, Ms. XXXX, states that he witnessed the troubling events that your uncle, XXXX XXXX, committed in your home; the problems and death threats had begun in 2010 after you and your husband refused this uncle's request to marry your then eight-year-old daughter.

propositions.text: The cousin states criminals attacked violently in 2015, with uncle involved, aiming to kill the appellant.
propositions.quote: He also states that in XXXX 2015, you were violently threatened at night by a group of criminals with firearms and blades. The uncle was a member of the group.

propositions.text: The cousin states criminals wore balaclavas, goal was to kill appellant, but appellant escaped; cousin was stabbed instead.
propositions.quote: Each member of this group wore a balaclava so that their faces were covered. Their goal was to kill you, Mr. XXXX, but you managed to escape. Your cousin also states that the criminals spent their anger by stabbing you, Ms. XXXX, thus causing serious injuries to your feet.

propositions.text: The cousin states the house remains a target and he initially avoided testifying to avoid conflict with uncle.
propositions.quote: Lastly, your cousin states that, since that time, your house, Ms. XXXX, has become the criminals' open target of threats. Before signing, your cousin states that, in the past, he did not want to testify because he wanted to avoid any conflict with the uncle.

paragraphs.summary: The cousin's written testimony describes violent threats and attacks by uncle and criminals, ongoing threats, and initial reluctance to testify.

propositions.text: The cousin's testimony mainly concerns facts before RPD rejection and adds no new specific information on ongoing threats.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this written testimony from your cousin concerns primarily facts that arose before the RPD rejected your refugee protection claims. Although he states that when he signed this testimony, your house was the criminals' open target, your cousin did not add any specific information to this matter.

propositions.text: The appellant previously stated criminals were still looking for them before the RPD.
propositions.quote: Just the same, you yourself stated before the RPD that these criminals were still looking for you.

propositions.text: Considering source and timing, the cousin's testimony lacks credibility.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, in considering the source of this testimony and the circumstances in which it came to light, namely after the RPD's rejection of your refugee protection claims, I find that this testimony lacks credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the cousin's testimony mainly repeats pre-RPD facts, adds no new details, and lacks credibility due to timing and source.

propositions.text: The cousin's testimony mainly confirms facts already analyzed and found not credible by RPD; it is inadmissible on appeal.
propositions.quote: Consequently, while being aware that your cousin states that he was unable to testify earlier, I conclude that this testimony is aimed at mainly confirming facts and allegations that have already been analyzed by the RPD, that credibility was lacking and there is no reason to admit it into evidence in your appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the cousin's testimony confirms previously analyzed facts lacking credibility and should not be admitted on appeal.

propositions.text: RAD Rules require appellants to provide detailed submissions on why an oral hearing should be held.
propositions.quote: The RAD Rules set out that the person who is the subject of the appeal must include in his memorandum full and detailed submissions regarding why the Division should hold a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD Rules require detailed submissions on why an oral hearing should be held.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the cousin's testimony corroborates appellant's claim of persecution by in-laws over forced marriage refusal.
propositions.quote: In your memorandum, you submitted that the written testimony from this cousin puts things in context regarding your credibility and he corroborates what you, Mr. XXXX, stated at the hearing, namely that you were persecuted by your in-laws for refusing the marriage proposal to your then eight-year-old daughter from an uncle who was 38 years old at the time.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the cousin's testimony corroborates the appellant's persecution claim regarding forced marriage refusal.

propositions.text: RAD decides if subsection 110(6) IRPA criteria for hearing are met, including admissibility of evidence.
propositions.quote: It is up to the RAD to determine whether the criteria set out in subsection 110(6) of the IRPA are satisfied or not.

propositions.text: Since the evidence submitted is inadmissible, holding an oral hearing is not possible.
propositions.quote: One of the criteria set out in this subsection is that the evidence submitted on appeal must be found admissible. However, I found that the evidence you submitted in your appeal is not admissible. Consequently, it is not possible to hold a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it cannot hold a hearing because the submitted evidence is inadmissible under IRPA 110(6).

propositions.text: RAD's role is not to reconsider refugee claims de novo but to determine if RPD erred as alleged.
propositions.quote: The role of the RAD is not to conduct a de novo consideration of a claim for refugee protection, but rather to determine whether the RPD erred as alleged.

propositions.text: The correctness standard of review applies to the RAD's independent analysis of the record.
propositions.quote: I have conducted an independent analysis of your record, and I am of the opinion that the correctness standard of review must be applied.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD reviews for errors, applying correctness standard, not re-hearing refugee claims anew.

propositions.text: RAD Rules require appellants to specify errors and their location in RPD decision or hearing record.
propositions.quote: The RAD Rules stipulate that the person who is the subject of the appeal must specify: i) the errors that are the grounds of the appeal, and ii) where the errors are located in the RPD decision, or in the transcript or in any recording of the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD Rules require appellants to specify errors and their location in the RPD decision or hearing record.

propositions.text: Appellant's counsel argues RPD's credibility findings are inconsistent and unfair regarding in-laws' threats and break-in.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the appellants' allegations regarding the criminals whom the in-laws had sent after them undermine their credibility. However, the appellants clearly testified that it was indeed the female appellant's 38-year-old uncle who wanted to marry their eight-year-old daughter and that he had the in-laws' overall blessing, as nearly the entire family of the female appellant agreed to this marriage, and it was the in-laws who, unable to make them change their minds, got the criminals to go after them. The panel notes a major inconsistency that undermines the appellants' credibility when they state that there was a connection between the break-in and the uncle's threats. The appellants clearly stated that they were threatened by the in-laws because of their resistance to the marriage. It is only normal for them to establish a link between the break-in and the threats from the in-laws. The panel is of the opinion that the appellants' testimony was not sincere, or credible regarding the allegations of visits made by the uncle. The appellants clearly testified at the hearing as to the number of times they met with the uncle and that he often acted through others. The panel itself recognized that the appellants were the victims of a break-in with photographic evidence of scars. This situation does not come under an application on humanitarian and compassionate considerations, as the appellants testified that it was the in-laws who carried out their threat with the break-in that almost claimed their lives.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant's counsel argues RPD's credibility findings are inconsistent and unfair regarding threats and break-in.

propositions.text: The appellant's submissions on RPD errors are unclear and appear to request a re-analysis of refugee claims.
propositions.quote: The submissions regarding the errors that, according to you, the RPD committed are all but clear and detailed. These submissions seem to me to be a request to analyze your refugee protection claims anew.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not commit the alleged errors after its own analysis.
propositions.quote: Regardless, according to my own analysis, the RPD did not commit the errors that you criticize it for.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's error submissions unclear and that RPD did not err after independent analysis.

propositions.text: Claimants are presumed truthful unless evidence shows inconsistencies or unsatisfactory explanations.
propositions.quote: When they swear to the truth of certain allegations, the refugee protection claimants are presumed to tell the truth. However, this presumption is challengeable where the evidence is inconsistent with the testimony or where the RPD is unsatisfied with the explanation for the inconsistencies.

propositions.text: RPD may draw negative inferences from implausibilities, inconsistencies, or omissions; overall evidence must be assessed.
propositions.quote: The RPD can draw negative inferences based on implausibilities, inconsistencies or omissions. It is the evidence overall that must be assessed.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites law that claimants are presumed truthful unless evidence contradicts, and RPD may draw negative inferences from inconsistencies.

propositions.text: RPD found contradictions and omissions undermining credibility and truthfulness of fear and risk allegations
propositions.quote: the RPD found your testimony and evidence raised a number of contradictions and omissions that undermined your credibility and cast doubt on the truthfulness of your allegations of fear and risk if you had to return to Angola.

propositions.text: RPD acknowledged burglary in 2015 but found no balance of probabilities that break-in related to allegations
propositions.quote: While acknowledging that you were burgled in XXXX 2015, the RPD found that you did not establish, on a balance of probabilities, that this break-in was related to your allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found contradictions undermining credibility and acknowledged a 2015 burglary but found no link to allegations, as reported by the RPD.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant not credible due to inconsistent allegations about feared persons
propositions.quote: Your inconsistent allegations regarding the person, the uncle, or persons, the in-laws whom you stated that you feared.

propositions.text: RPD distinguished hearing rumours of threats from being directly threatened by criminals
propositions.quote: The difference between hearing rumours of threats and being directly threatened by criminals.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's testimony vague about events and uncle's actions in home country
propositions.quote: Your vague testimony and statements regarding what exactly transpired in your country and regarding the facts and actions of the uncle whom you claim that you fear.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant not credible due to inconsistent allegations, difference between rumours and direct threats, and vague testimony about events and uncle.

propositions.text: RPD did not commit the errors criticized by the appellant
propositions.quote: According to my own analysis of your record, the RPD did not commit the errors that you criticize it for.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds that the RPD did not commit the errors the appellant criticizes.

propositions.text: RPD analyzed photographs and recognized break-in and injuries but found no link to allegations
propositions.quote: It recognized that you were undoubtedly the victims of a break-in and that you, Madam, sustained injuries, but it nevertheless found that you did not establish that these events stemmed from your allegations

propositions.text: RPD found appellant not credible regarding allegations about uncle wanting to marry daughter
propositions.quote: As the RPD found that you were not credible regarding these allegations, it could not grant them any weight.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence is not assessed in isolation from the overall claim; weight is persuasiveness compared to other evidence
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence is not assessed in isolation from the overall claim. The weight of evidence is the persuasiveness of some evidence in comparison with other evidence.

propositions.text: Court's own analysis finds no errors by the RPD
propositions.quote: According to my own analysis of the record, the RPD did not commit any errors.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD analyzed evidence properly, found no credibility, and committed no errors in weighing evidence.

propositions.text: Confirms RPD's determination that appellant and children did not establish well-founded fear or risk under IRPA sections 96 and 97
propositions.quote: I confirm the RPD's determination, that is, that you and your minor children did not establish that you have a well-founded fear of persecution within the meaning of section 96 or that you would be subjected to a risk within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA, if you had to return to live in Angola.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's determination that appellant and children did not establish well-founded fear or risk under IRPA.

propositions.text: Dismisses the appeal
propositions.quote: Your appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
